fields.text: Day to night between two keyframes. Muse paints the scene at midday, Muse Edit repaints the same shot at night, and MiniMax H3 Max gets both: the day still on its image port and the night still on its end-frame port, so the clip has to start on one and land on the other. The same trick works for any before/after (seasons, a room before and after, a bare plot and a finished house). Inspired by @Audrius1454663's open-source rebuild of Higgsfield's VFX presets (Day→Night and more) on the Comfy Developer Platform (https://x.com/Audrius1454663/status/2111177673842012349).

A handmade paper-craft miniature seaside village at bright midday, wide eye-level view from across the little harbor: six small houses made of folded colored card with dark empty windows, a red-and-white striped paper lighthouse on the rocks at the right with its lamp off, two folded paper boats on layered blue paper waves, a cardboard pier, round paper trees, a paper sun high in a clear blue sky. Crisp paper folds and visible card texture, soft tabletop-diorama light with short shadows, no people, no animals, no text.

Repaint this exact scene at night. Keep the same camera, framing and every house, tree, boat, pier and the lighthouse in exactly the same place and shape, still made of paper and card. Change only the light: a deep navy night sky with small paper stars and a paper crescent moon in place of the sun, warm yellow light glowing in every house window, the lighthouse lamp switched on with a soft beam across the water, warm reflections on the paper waves. No people, no animals, no text.

Locked-off camera, a smooth tabletop timelapse from midday to night. The paper sun sinks behind the village, shadows stretch long across the card, the sky warms to orange and pink and then deepens to navy blue, the house windows light up one by one, the lighthouse lamp switches on and its beam sweeps over the water, the paper stars appear. The camera never moves and nothing new enters the scene. No people, no text.
